question.text: Will the winner of the 2026 American League MVP Award be a unanimous selection?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the player announced as the 2026 American League Most Valuable Player (announcement scheduled for November 12, 2026) is listed first on every ballot in the official BBWAA tally, and No otherwise. Resolution is based on the BBWAA's official 2026 AL MVP announcement and its accompanying full ballot breakdown, published on and linked from the BBWAA Annual Awards page (https://bbwaa.com/awards). If that page is unavailable or does not report first-place vote totals, the official BBWAA vote count as reported by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) will be used.
question.fine_print: The AL MVP is voted on by 30 BBWAA members (two writers from each of the 15 American League cities). If fewer than 30 ballots are included in the official tally, the question resolves Yes only if the winner is listed first on every ballot counted.

research:
## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-02: The BBWAA Annual Awards page (bbwaa.com/awards) lists only dates for 2026: AL and NL MVP on Nov. 12, Cy Young Nov. 11, Manager of the Year Nov. 10, Rookie of the Year Nov. 9. It shows no 2026 winners, finalists or ballots yet. The latest MVP winners listed are from 2025: Aaron Judge (AL) and Shohei Ohtani (NL). [BBWAA](https://bbwaa.com/awards)
- Ballots were cast before the postseason, so the result is already fixed. It just hasn't been published.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. I could not find an official BBWAA finalist list for 2026. In 2025 the finalists were announced in early November, so 2026's may come within days. Kalshi's finalist market is still trading, which suggests they hadn't been released as of Nov. 2.
- Alvarez is the overwhelming favorite to win. Whether he wins unanimously is not settled.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-02: Bleacher Report's team-by-team picks name Alvarez the Astros' MVP (.316, 42 HR). [Bleacher Report](https://bleacherreport.com/articles/25527611-picking-every-mlb-teams-mvp-cy-young-and-rookie-year-2026)
- 2026-10-28: Alvarez won the Players Choice AL Outstanding Player award. In the same article, FanGraphs has Bobby Witt Jr. leading position players in WAR at 7.0, with Alvarez at 6.8. Witt's case rests on defense and baserunning, despite a career-low 18 HR. Alvarez trails Pete Alonso in both HR and RBI. Witt leading in fWAR is a plausible reason a few voters could put him first. [Bleacher Report](https://bleacherreport.com/articles/25521625-mlb-players-choice-awards-2026-results-winners-and-reaction)
- 2026-09-22: MLB.com's final poll of 38 staff:

| Player | First-place votes | Points |
|---|---|---|
| Alvarez | 29 | 181 |
| Caminero | 7 | 149 |
| Witt | 1 | 62 |
| Schlittler | 1 | 60 |

  So about 24% of first-place votes went to someone other than Alvarez. The poll noted his late slump: .264 with a .840 OPS over his previous 41 games, and 3 HR and 5 RBI in 16 September games. He still led the AL in wRC+ (179) by 27 or more points. [MLB.com](https://www.mlb.com/news/yordan-alvarez-pete-crow-armstrong-lead-final-2026-mvp-poll)
- 2026-08-25: Bleacher Report had Witt leading AL players in WAR at that point, 6.2 to Alvarez's 5.8. [Bleacher Report](https://bleacherreport.com/articles/25481436-ranking-mlbs-top-10-al-and-nl-mvp-candidates-2026)
- Search summaries mention a separate MLB.com poll where Alvarez had 34 first-place votes. I could not confirm which poll or date that was. [Yahoo](https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/yordan-alvarez-dominates-al-mvp-182155558.html)

## 4. Base rates
AL MVP first-place votes, from my own knowledge of recent BBWAA results (not fetched this session):

| Year | Winner | First-place votes | Unanimous? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2025 | Judge | 17/30 | No |
| 2024 | Judge | 30/30 | Yes |
| 2023 | Ohtani | 30/30 | Yes |
| 2022 | Judge | 28/30 | No |
| 2021 | Ohtani | 30/30 | Yes |
| 2020 | Abreu | 21/30 | No |
| 2019 | Trout | 17/30 | No |
| 2018 | Betts | 28/30 | No |
| 2017 | Altuve | 27/30 | No |
| 2016 | Trout | 19/30 | No |
| 2015 | Donaldson | 23/30 | No |
| 2014 | Trout | 30/30 | Yes |

- That is 4 of the last 12 AL MVPs (about 33%) and 3 of the last 5.
- Even heavy favorites have lost a vote or two (Judge in 2022, Betts in 2018).
- Every recent unanimous winner was also the clear WAR leader (Ohtani as a two-way player, Judge in 2024). In 2026 Alvarez does not lead in fWAR (Witt is ahead) and is mainly a DH.

## 5. Other forecasts
- 2026-11-02 (Kalshi, 17:11 UTC), AL MVP winner: Alvarez 0.96, Schlittler 0.02, everyone else 0.01 or less. This prices who wins, not whether it is unanimous.
- 2026-11-02 (Kalshi), AL MVP finalists: Alvarez 0.94, Caminero 0.85, Witt 0.73, Schlittler 0.40, Alonso 0.23.
- I could not find a Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on whether the AL MVP will be unanimous. Covers cited Polymarket at Alvarez 97%, Caminero 3%. [Covers](https://www.covers.com/mlb/mvp-odds)
- Expert proxy: the MLB.com staff poll was not unanimous (29 of 38).

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Early November (date unconfirmed): BBWAA top-three finalists announced on MLB Network. If Alvarez is the only clear favorite, the other two names may hint at how votes split.
- Nov. 5: Silver Slugger finalists. These have no bearing on the vote, which is already cast.
- Nov. 9 to 11: the other BBWAA awards.
- Nov. 12, 7 p.m. ET: AL MVP announced, with full ballots posted by the BBWAA and MLB.com.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 10 days remain: the result is announced Nov. 12, 2026, with ballots already cast before the postseason. Yes requires the AL MVP winner, almost surely Alvarez, to be listed first on all 30 BBWAA ballots.

(b) The ballots are fixed, so there is no status quo in the usual sense. The default expectation for a favorite with a non-dominant profile is a clear win that is not unanimous.

(c) Base rate: 4 of the last 12 AL MVPs were unanimous (about 33%), and 3 of the last 5. All the unanimous winners were clear WAR leaders with historic or two-way seasons (Ohtani in 2021 and 2023, Judge in 2024, Trout in 2014). Conditioned on "favorite but not the WAR leader, and a DH," the rate is much lower: Judge with 62 HR in 2022 and Betts in 2018 each still lost two votes.

(d) Evidence:
- **For Yes:**
  - Alvarez led the majors in OBP, SLG, OPS and walks, won the batting title, and led the AL in wRC+ by 27 or more points.
  - Markets give him about 96-97% to win (Kalshi, Nov. 2).
  - He won the Players Choice AL Outstanding Player award (Oct. 28).
- **For No:**
  - The MLB.com final poll on Sept. 22 gave Alvarez only 29 of 38 first-place votes, with 7 going to Caminero, 1 to Witt and 1 to Schlittler.
  - FanGraphs has Witt ahead in WAR, 7.0 to 6.8 (Oct. 28).
  - Alvarez is mainly a DH and trails Alonso in both HR and RBI.
  - He slumped badly late: 3 HR in 16 September games.
  - Kalshi prices Caminero (0.85) and Witt (0.73) as likely finalists, which suggests real support for both.

(e) No scenario: Alvarez wins with about 24-27 first-place votes. Some voters reward Witt's defense and fWAR lead, or Caminero's 42 HR at third base, and a few penalize the DH profile and late slump. Yes scenario: the writers treat Alvarez's rate-stat dominance as decisive, and all 30 put him first despite the poll split.

(f) I start from 33% and move down sharply. The expert poll was clearly split, roughly a quarter of first-place votes going elsewhere, unlike the poll pattern in recent unanimous years. Alvarez also lacks a WAR lead and plays DH, which even more dominant candidates (Judge 2022, Betts 2018) could not overcome. The win market does not price unanimity, so it is not an anchor here. I land at about 10%.

Probability: 10%

(a) About 10 days remain. The AL MVP is announced November 12, 2026, and full ballots are posted that night. Ballots were cast before the postseason, so the result is already fixed but not public. For Yes, the winner, almost certainly Yordan Alvarez, must be listed first on all 30 BBWAA ballots.

(b) The status quo is unclear, because the outcome is fixed but unknown. The most likely shape is a decisive Alvarez win with a handful of first-place votes going to Caminero, Witt or Schlittler. That would be a No.

(c) Base rate: 4 of the last 12 AL MVPs were unanimous, about 33%, and 3 of the last 5 were. The more relevant reference class is narrower: winners who were heavy favorites but not clearly the WAR leader, and who were DHs or had a split expert consensus. Those rarely sweep. Judge in 2022 lost two first-place votes even with 62 HR and a clear WAR lead. In that narrower class, unanimity looks closer to 10-15%.

(d) Evidence:
- **For Yes:**
  - Kalshi had Alvarez at 0.96 to win on 2026-11-02, and Polymarket at about 97%.
  - Alvarez led the majors in OBP, SLG and OPS, won the batting title and led the AL in wRC+ by 27 or more points.
  - He won the Players Choice AL Outstanding Player award on 2026-10-28.
- **For No:**
  - MLB.com's final poll on 2026-09-22 gave Alvarez only 29 of 38 first-place votes, with Caminero getting 7.
  - FanGraphs WAR has Witt ahead, 7.0 to 6.8 (reported 2026-10-28).
  - Alvarez is mainly a DH, slumped in September (3 HR in 16 games) and trails Alonso in HR and RBI.
  - The Kalshi finalist market sees Caminero at 0.85 and Witt at 0.73 as credible alternatives.

(e) Scenarios:
- **No:** Two or three WAR-focused writers put Witt first for his defense and baserunning, and a couple of others pick Caminero for his 42 HR at third base. Alvarez wins about 25-5.
- **Yes:** Writers treat Alvarez's rate-stat dominance and batting title as overwhelming, ignore the September slump, and all 30 list him first, as happened with Judge in 2024.

(f) I start at about 33% from the raw base rate. I move down sharply because the expert poll showed about 24% of first-place votes going elsewhere, the WAR lead belongs to someone else, and Alvarez is a DH. Every recent unanimous winner was the clear WAR leader with near-unanimous expert polls. No market prices unanimity directly, and a 96-97% win price is consistent with a decisive but split vote. I land around 11%.

Probability: 11%

(a) About 10 days remain. The AL MVP is announced November 12, 2026, with full ballots published that night. The ballots were cast before the postseason, so the outcome is already fixed but not yet public. For Yes, the announced winner (almost certainly Yordan Alvarez) must be listed first on all 30 BBWAA ballots.

(b) If nothing changed, the status quo is a non-unanimous Alvarez win. Every available expert proxy shows a split in first-place votes.

(c) Base rate: 4 of the last 12 AL MVPs were unanimous (about 33%). If I limit the reference class to clear favorites who were not also the dominant WAR leader, the rate is lower. Judge in 2022 (28/30), Betts in 2018 (28/30) and Altuve in 2017 (27/30) were heavy favorites and still not unanimous. Every recent unanimous winner, Ohtani in 2021 and 2023 and Judge in 2024, was the runaway WAR leader. For favorites without a WAR edge, I estimate a base rate of about 15-20%.

(d) Evidence for Yes:
- Prediction markets give Alvarez a 96-97% chance to win (Kalshi and Polymarket, Nov. 2).
- He leads the AL in wRC+ by 27 or more points and led the majors in OBP, slugging and OPS.
- He won the Players Choice AL Outstanding Player award (Oct. 28).

Evidence for No:
- The MLB.com staff poll (Sept. 22) gave Alvarez only 29 of 38 first-place votes, with 7 going to Caminero and 1 each to Witt and Schlittler.
- That poll noted Alvarez's late slump: a .840 OPS over his last 41 games, and 3 HR in 16 September games.
- Witt leads in fWAR, 7.0 to 6.8 (Oct. 28).
- Alvarez is primarily a DH and trails Alonso in HR and RBI.

(e) No scenario: One or more of the 30 writers puts Witt first for his defense and fWAR edge, or picks Caminero, Alonso or Schlittler. Alvarez wins something like 26 of 30 first-place votes.

Yes scenario: The writers converge on Alvarez's overwhelming offensive lead, the way they did for recent clear favorites, and all 30 vote him first.

(f) I start from about 17% for a favorite without a WAR edge. I move down because of the specific split in the staff poll. If roughly 24% of experts chose someone else, the chance that all 30 BBWAA voters pick Alvarez is small, even allowing that BBWAA voters are more correlated with each other than poll respondents are. A DH without the WAR lead is also exactly the profile that draws protest votes. There is no direct market on unanimity. I land at about 9%.

Probability: 9%

**(a) Time left and what Yes requires**
The result is known on Nov. 12, 2026, about 10 days from now. Ballots are already locked. Yes requires the announced 2026 AL MVP to be first on all 30 BBWAA ballots in the official breakdown.

**(b) Status quo outcome**
Alvarez wins (about 96% on Kalshi), but nothing points to a sweep. With no new information, the default is a non-unanimous Alvarez win, which resolves No.

**(c) Base rate**
AL MVP unanimity since 2014 is 4 of 12, about 33%. Unanimous winners (Trout 2014, Ohtani 2021 and 2023, Judge 2024) had overwhelming WAR leads. Conditioning on a winner without a WAR edge, the rate is much lower, roughly 10% or less.

**(d) Strongest evidence**
- For Yes:
  - Alvarez leads the majors in OBP, SLG and OPS, won the batting title, and leads the AL in total bases and extra-base hits.
  - Markets price him at about 96-97% to win (Kalshi Nov. 2; chanceindex Oct. 27), so he is a dominant favorite.
  - ESPN had him at -6000 late in the season.
- For No:
  - In MLB.com's final expert poll (Sept. 22), only 29 of 38 picked him first. Caminero got 7 first-place votes, Witt 1 and Schlittler 1.
  - His first-place share fell from 34 of 37 in the prior poll.
  - He slumped late, hitting .264 with an .840 OPS over his last 41 games.
  - He is tied with Witt for the AL lead in FanGraphs WAR (6.8), and Witt led the poll in WAR and defense.
  - He is a primary DH, a profile some voters discount.
  - Caminero had an "MVP moment" with a walk-off homer that clinched a Rays playoff spot.

**(e) Scenarios**
- No: Several BBWAA writers, especially from Tampa Bay, Kansas City or WAR-focused outlets, put Caminero or Witt first. Alvarez wins with something like 22-27 first-place votes.
- Yes: Voters treat Alvarez's rate-stat dominance as decisive, as with Ohtani's unanimous 2024 NL award as a DH. All 30 put him first despite the expert-poll dissent.

**(f) Moving from the base rate to my forecast**
I start at 33% and move down sharply. Proxy expert polls usually predict BBWAA consensus fairly well. A 24% dissent rate in that poll, a WAR tie, a DH profile and a late slump make 30 of 30 unlikely. Even near-consensus favorites like Betts (2018) and Judge (2022) dropped two votes. I keep a small tail for writers consolidating behind a clear favorite.
